key_insight: A variational latent neural field can jointly predict reduced-order dynamics, quantify uncertainty, and exactly preserve conservation laws by embedding the solution in a divergence-free solution-flux manifold.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical surrogate modeling route for CFD and conservation-law systems where speed, robustness to sparse/noisy data, and physically consistent forecasts all matter.
method: Uses Gaussian process-inspired latent neural field surrogates for uncertainty-aware reduced-order modeling.
Compares three variants: IRS-UQ (unconstrained), PI-IRS-UQ (physics-informed), and ECLEIRS-UQ (conservation-structure-preserving).
Enforces exact conservation via a space-time divergence-free representation of the solution-flux field.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on three parameterized nonlinear benchmarks—1-D advection, 2-D Euler, and 2-D shallow water—showing accurate predictions with uncertainty estimates and robustness under sparse/noisy training data.
watch_item: The conservation-preserving formulation may add implementation complexity and could require careful numerical treatment to scale to higher-dimensional or more complex geometries.
paper_title: Structure-preserving variational neural fields: Uncertainty-quantified reduced-order modeling of nonlinear conservation laws
